questions.prompt: Identify one type of resource hardware consideration when developing a Human Computer Interface (HCI).
questions.markSchemeHint: Memory (RAM), processing power (CPU), storage capacity, battery/power consumption.

questions.scenarioContext: An online booking system is being created for a sports centre. An app is being developed to book the facilities which include a gym, tennis courts and indoor football pitches. Customers will need to use the app to register with the sports centre and book the facilities.
questions.prompt: Identify two digital devices that this app could be used on.
questions.markSchemeHint: Any two: smartphone, tablet, smartwatch, laptop/PC (if web/app supported).

questions.scenarioContext: Customers need to set up Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) for using the sports centre app.
questions.prompt: Describe how 2FA works.
questions.markSchemeHint: Requires two separate forms of identity verification to log in (1), e.g., entering a username/password (something you know) followed by a one-time code sent by SMS/authenticator app or a biometric scan (something you have/are) (1).

questions.scenarioContext: A sports centre booking app will include a Human Computer Interface (HCI).
questions.prompt: Explain one advantage to the customer of the booking app having an HCI.
questions.markSchemeHint: 1 mark advantage + 1 mark expansion: makes it easy/intuitive to view availability and book courts/gym slots anytime without phoning or queuing; clear visual feedback reduces booking errors.

questions.scenarioContext: Designing the sports centre booking app HCI.
questions.prompt: Explain one reason why display size should be considered when designing the booking app HCI.
questions.markSchemeHint: 1 mark point + 1 mark expansion: smartphones have smaller screens than tablets, so text, buttons, and booking calendars must scale/fit cleanly without overcrowding, excessive scrolling, or unreadable text.

questions.scenarioContext: Interacting with the sports centre booking app HCI.
questions.prompt: Explain one advantage to the customer of using voice to interact with the booking app HCI.
questions.markSchemeHint: 1 mark point + 1 mark expansion: hands-free convenience (e.g., booking a class while walking/driving/packing gym kit), faster than typing on a small keyboard, or supports accessibility for visually/motor-impaired customers.

questions.prompt: Other than voice, describe one other user interaction method that could be used with the HCI.
questions.markSchemeHint: 1 mark method + 1 mark description of how it works: e.g., Touch (tapping/swiping buttons and date pickers directly on the screen), Keyboard (typing details/search terms), Gesture (tilting/pinching to navigate), Mouse/Pointer.

questions.scenarioContext: After a customer logs in to the sports centre app, the first screen they see is the booking screen dashboard.
questions.prompt: Identify two advantages of using a visualisation diagram to plan the booking screen dashboard.
questions.markSchemeHint: Any two: clearly shows final look/colours/fonts/layout to the client before coding; easy/cheap to amend designs early; gives developers an exact blueprint to follow; helps check layout isn't cluttered.

questions.scenarioContext:
The information that can be shown on the sports centre booking screen dashboard includes:
• username and photograph
• making a booking
• current bookings
• past bookings.
questions.prompt:
Create a visualisation diagram to plan the content and layout of the booking screen dashboard.
Marks will be awarded for: content; layout.
questions.markSchemeHint: Up to 4 marks Content (sports centre title/logo, username & profile photo area, clear sections/buttons for Make a Booking, Current Bookings, Past Bookings, annotations for colours/fonts/images/house style) and up to 4 marks Layout (clear mobile app boundary, clean visual hierarchy, balanced spacing, readable navigation).

questions.scenarioContext:
When a customer makes a booking they enter data with these requirements:
• Activity: fitness gym, badminton, football, yoga.
• Bookings can only be a maximum of 4 weeks in advance.
• Customers must confirm their contact email address.
questions.prompt: Complete the table to show the data validation tool that would be used for each data field in the app. Justify each of your choices.
questions.markSchemeHint: 3 marks per row (1 validation tool + 2 justification): Activity -> Lookup / Limited choice (drop-down list / radio buttons) because only 4 fixed activities exist, preventing spelling mistakes; Date -> Range check (or Format check) to enforce bookings cannot exceed 4 weeks in advance (or DD/MM/YYYY); Contact email address -> Format check / Input mask (checks for '@' and domain) or Presence check (ensures email is entered for confirmation).

questions.scenarioContext: After a customer has signed up to use the sports centre app they will receive instructions about how to use it through a multimedia distribution channel.
questions.prompt: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to the customer of receiving the app instructions through a multimedia distribution channel.
questions.markSchemeHint: Advantage (2): combines video/audio/graphics/text making step-by-step booking instructions easier and more engaging to follow than plain text, can pause/replay anytime. Disadvantage (2): requires internet/bandwidth and a capable device (uses mobile data), may not be accessible without captions/audio controls, or cannot be read offline.

questions.scenarioContext: Receiving app instructions via a multimedia distribution channel.
questions.prompt: Identify two types of digital communication that could be used with the multimedia distribution channel.
questions.markSchemeHint: Any two: video, animation, podcast/audio, digital presentation, interactive website/webinar, social media post, infographic.

questions.scenarioContext: When a booking is made through the sports centre app, the app stores the data in a spreadsheet stored in the cloud.
questions.prompt: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to the sports centre of storing the data in the cloud.
questions.markSchemeHint: Advantage (2): staff can access live booking sheets from any location/device, scalable storage as memberships grow, automatic provider backups. Disadvantage (2): relies on continuous internet connection to view bookings, ongoing subscription fees, data security/privacy reliance on third-party provider.

questions.scenarioContext: The sports centre keeps a physical secure backup of the booking data.
questions.prompt: Describe how Network-Attached Storage (NAS) could be used to store the physical secure backup of the data.
questions.markSchemeHint: A dedicated storage device connected directly to the sports centre's local network (1) that automatically/regularly copies booking files onto local hard drives/RAID accessible to authorised staff even if the internet fails (1).

questions.scenarioContext: Physical secure backups of sports centre booking data.
questions.prompt: Identify two other external storage devices that could be used to store the secure backup of the data.
questions.markSchemeHint: Any two: external hard disk drive (HDD), external solid-state drive (SSD), USB flash drive, magnetic tape, SD card, optical disc.

questions.scenarioContext: Choose one term from: Anti-virus, Encryption, RFID, Username.
questions.prompt:
Complete the following sentence:
.............................................. is a physical prevention measure.
questions.markSchemeHint: RFID (1 mark).

questions.scenarioContext:
A sports centre wants to manage its buildings, pitches and equipment using the Internet of Everything (IoE), including smart devices, to manage:
• access to the gym and pitches
• use of the heating and lighting
• security of the buildings
• maintenance of the equipment.
questions.prompt:
Discuss the suitability of using the IoE to manage the sports centre's buildings, pitches and equipment.

In your answer you must consider:
• the purpose of the IoE for the sports centre
• advantages of using the IoE to the sports centre
• disadvantages of using the IoE to the sports centre.
questions.markSchemeHint: OCR 9-mark Level of Response (L1: 1–3, L2: 4–6, L3: 7–9). Purpose: connect sensors, smart locks, lighting/HVAC, CCTV, and gym machines to automate operations and collect live data. Advantages: lower energy bills (motion-triggered lights/heating), automated RFID/app access reduces staffing costs, proactive maintenance alerts prevent machine downtime, 24/7 smart security alerts. Disadvantages: high upfront installation cost, reliance on Wi-Fi/power (outage locks out users), cyber-security attack surface across many IoT devices, staff training/ongoing maintenance. Reasoned conclusion.
